# Eye Rest

> A calm, hand-painted macOS menu-bar app that enforces the 20-20-20 eye-rest rule with full-screen painterly break scenes. Free to start; Pro is a one-time $14.99 (no subscription), macOS 14+.

Eye Rest reminds knowledge workers to rest their eyes on the 20-20-20 rule and turns each break into a hand-painted scene they'll actually take. A gentle heads-up precedes every break, and any break can be skipped or snoozed, so it never ambushes you. Differentiator: beauty drives adherence — unlike utilitarian break apps (LookAway, Time Out, Stretchly) that get uninstalled.

## Guides & comparisons
- [The 20-20-20 rule: why you never actually keep it](https://hungranger.github.io/eyerest/20-20-20-rule.html): what the rule is, why adherence fails (willpower + naggy apps), and what makes a break stick
- [Digital eye strain on a Mac](https://hungranger.github.io/eyerest/digital-eye-strain-mac.html): why long Mac sessions hurt your eyes (reduced blinking, fixed focus) and the 20-20-20 fix
- [Best Mac eye-strain & break apps (2026)](https://hungranger.github.io/eyerest/best-mac-eye-strain-apps.html): honest buyer's guide ranking Eye Rest, LookAway, Stretchly, Time Out, f.lux
- [Eye Rest vs LookAway](https://hungranger.github.io/eyerest/vs-lookaway.html): hand-painted break + flat $14.99 one-time vs highly configurable dimming + per-device tiers
- [Eye Rest vs Stretchly](https://hungranger.github.io/eyerest/eye-rest-vs-stretchly.html): paid, Mac-native, hand-painted vs free, open-source, cross-platform
- [Eye Rest vs Time Out](https://hungranger.github.io/eyerest/eye-rest-vs-time-out.html): focused 20-20-20 + painterly scenes vs a highly configurable general break timer
- [Founder story](https://hungranger.github.io/eyerest/story.html): why the maker quit every break app and painted one he'd actually keep

## Positioning
- Beauty drives adherence: the break is a hand-painted scene you look forward to, not a pop-up you dismiss — so you actually take it.
- Audience: Mac knowledge workers (developers, designers, writers, analysts) with digital eye strain who have uninstalled naggy break apps before.
- vs alternatives: differs from LookAway, Time Out, and Stretchly on the hand-painted full-screen break scene and a flat one-time $14.99 (no per-device tiers, no subscription).
- Free tier includes the pre-break heads-up and skip/snooze; Pro adds smart auto-pause (video calls, browser video, idle), all six scenes, office hours, and stats.
